---
title: "Logging"
subtitle: "One file per application start, and the one place a failed sync explains itself"
---

Every start of the application opens a **new log file** and keeps it for the
life of the process. The file is the full record of what the run did: the
Moodle handshake, one line per web-service call, how many courses and documents
each stage retrieved, every warning, and every traceback.

The reason it exists is the sync. It runs in a background thread, reports to
the loading screen as five stage labels, and nothing else — so when a stage
said *failed* there was no record of what had happened before it. A one-line
`detail` on a progress bar is not enough to tell an expired token from a
rate-limited model pass from a file the download endpoint refused.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
`src/logs.py` is the whole implementation, and
[`src/config.py`](#configuration) holds every setting. Nothing in it raises: a
read-only or missing log directory costs the session its file and says so on
the terminal, but never stops the application.
:::

## Where it goes

```
logs/modboard-20261014-202414-30600.log
      ^        ^              ^
      |        |              └── pid, so two starts in one second stay apart
      |        └── local time the process started (LOG_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT)
      └── LOG_FILENAME_TEMPLATE
```

`logs/` is gitignored — a log belongs to the run that produced it, not to the
repository. `python app.py --log-dir /somewhere/else` moves it, and the startup
banner prints the path it chose:

```bash
$ uv run python app.py
Modboard on http://127.0.0.1:5000
  database /Users/fynnfischer/Projects/moodle_single_page/moodle.sqlite -- 5 course(s)
  logging to /Users/fynnfischer/Projects/moodle_single_page/logs/modboard-20261014-202414-30600.log
```

## Two destinations, different levels

The handlers filter, not the loggers. The root logger sits at `DEBUG` and each
handler decides what it keeps, because a level on the logger would cap both.

| | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| The file | `DEBUG` | Everything, including one line per web-service call and per downloaded file |
| The terminal | `WARNING` | The loading screen polls twice a second; an `INFO` terminal would bury the startup banner |

So the terminal stays as quiet as it was before logging existed — the banner,
then nothing unless something is actually wrong. Raise `LOG_FILE_LEVEL` to
`"INFO"` to drop the per-call lines from the file; lower `LOG_CONSOLE_LEVEL` to
`"DEBUG"` to watch a run live.

Third-party loggers are pinned in `LOG_QUIET_LOGGERS`, since the root sitting
at `DEBUG` otherwise invites all of them in:

| Logger | Pinned to | Otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| `werkzeug` | `WARNING` | One line per request — and the loading screen polls `/api/sync` continuously |
| `urllib3`, `httpx`, `httpcore` | `WARNING` | One line per connection, per file downloaded |
| `keyring` | `WARNING` | Lists every credential backend on the machine on the first lookup |
| `anthropic` | `INFO` | Retries and rate-limit waits are worth keeping |

## The logger tree

Every module's logger hangs off `modboard`, so one level change covers the
application and ours stay separable from everybody else's:

```python
from ..logs import get_logger

log = get_logger("harvest")        # -> modboard.harvest
```

| Logger | Records |
|---|---|
| `modboard.session` | The header: when, which Python, which database and site |
| `modboard.app` | App construction, the address it serves on, the course count |
| `modboard.http` | The two writes (`POST /api/key`, `POST /api/sync`) and 404s. Reads are not logged — they are polled |
| `modboard.sync` | Stage start/finish/fail with durations, and the run's own summary |
| `modboard.sync.login`, `.harvest`, `.screen`, `.extract` | What each stage's own progress messages said |
| `modboard.moodle.auth` | Public config, launch, token signature verification |
| `modboard.moodle.client` | One line per web-service call: function, result size, elapsed. Refusals and network errors at `ERROR` |
| `modboard.moodle.session` | Connection route and identity, course counts, per-activity polling |
| `modboard.documents` | Per-course activity counts as documents are built |
| `modboard.harvest` | Per-file downloads and skips, warnings, harvest totals |
| `modboard.corpus.reader` | Which corpus is being read, and when it was harvested |
| `modboard.screen`, `modboard.extract` | Model, workers, per-course results, totals with token usage |
| `modboard.storage` | Store opens, drops, document and account writes |
| `modboard.pipeline` | Anything a default `on_message` printed (see [below](#the-on_message-bridge)) |

## The `on_message` bridge

Each pipeline class reports progress through an `on_message` callback so it
need not know where its output goes. There were two callers and both were
lossy: a script passed `print`, and the web app passed `lambda m: None` —
throwing every progress line away precisely when nobody was watching a
terminal.

Both now go somewhere:

| Caller | `on_message` | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Script, notebook | `logs.echo` (the default) | Prints **and** logs, so interactive use is unchanged |
| The background sync | `logs.message_sink("sync.harvest")` | Logs only — there is no terminal to print to |

That is why the excerpt above carries lines like
`modboard.sync.login  Using the stored token (…)`: the stage's own words, kept
because the stage no longer talks into a void.

```python
# src/app/jobs.py
harvester = UnstructuredHarvester(
    session, root=DEFAULT_CORPUS_ROOT, fresh=True,
    on_message=message_sink("sync.harvest"),
)
```

## Crashes nobody caught

`logs.configure()` installs `sys.excepthook` **and**
`threading.excepthook`. The sync is a thread, so without the second one a
failure outside a stage's own `try` would print to a terminal nobody reads and
leave the log with no trace of why the run stopped. With it:

``` {.default}
20:22:13 ERROR    modboard.sync              sync aborted by an unhandled error
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../src/app/jobs.py", line 199, in _sync
    store = CourseStore(self.db, fresh=True)
  File ".../src/storage/sqlite.py", line 140, in __init__
    log.info("dropped %s before opening it", ", ".join(self.dropped))
TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, PosixPath found
20:22:13 ERROR    modboard.sync              sync finished with an error after 12.1s: TypeError: ...
```

That really happened, on the first run after logging was added, and it is a
fair advertisement for the feature: the stage list on screen said only
*Fetching courses & activities — failed*.

## What is never logged

| Secret | Treatment |
|---|---|
| The Anthropic API key | Referred to, never written. `POST /api/key` logs *that* a key was stored, not the key |
| The login passport | Never logged. `begin_login` logs the base `launch.php` URL, not the signed one that carries it |
| The web-service token | **Masked only.** `TokenMask` renders it as `7280...1a1a (32 chars)` |
| Request bodies | Never. `modboard.moodle.client` logs the function name and the *size* of the answer, never its contents |

The masked token is the one thing to be aware of: four leading and four
trailing characters of a 32-character token appear in the file. That is the
project's existing display format, not a logging decision, but it means a log
file is not something to paste into a public issue unedited.

## Reading a run

```bash
# the newest session
less "$(ls -t logs/*.log | head -1)"

# the stage-level story, without the per-call noise
grep "modboard.sync " logs/modboard-*.log

# everything that went wrong
grep -E "WARNING|ERROR|CRITICAL" logs/modboard-*.log

# what the Moodle conversation cost
grep "modboard.moodle.client" logs/modboard-*.log | wc -l

# the slow calls
grep -oE "modboard.moodle.client.*in [0-9]+\.[0-9]+s" logs/*.log | sort -t' ' -k2 -rn | head
```

## Configuration

Everything is in the *Session logging* section of `src/config.py`.

| Setting | Default | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `LOG_DIR` | `PROJECT_ROOT / "logs"` | Where session files go; `--log-dir` overrides it |
| `LOG_ROOT_NAME` | `"modboard"` | The logger every module hangs off |
| `LOG_FILENAME_TEMPLATE` | `"modboard-{started}-{pid}.log"` | Also the glob that finds old sessions to prune |
| `LOG_TIMESTAMP_FORMAT` | `"%Y%m%d-%H%M%S"` | Fixed width, so name order *is* time order |
| `LOG_FILE_LEVEL` | `"DEBUG"` | Raise to `"INFO"` to drop the per-call lines |
| `LOG_CONSOLE_LEVEL` | `"WARNING"` | Lower to `"INFO"` to watch a run live |
| `LOG_FORMAT`, `LOG_DATE_FORMAT` | time, level, logger, message | |
| `LOG_KEEP_SESSIONS` | `20` | Sessions kept; `None` keeps every one |
| `LOG_QUIET_LOGGERS` | see above | Third-party loggers and the level they are pinned to |

**Retention** happens on startup, before the new file is opened: the directory
is listed, sorted by name — which is sorted by time, because the timestamp is
fixed width — and the oldest deleted until there is room for one more. Reading
the directory is the whole mechanism; there is no index to keep in step, and
nothing that does not match `LOG_FILENAME_TEMPLATE` is ever touched.

## Using it outside the web app

`app.py` calls `configure()` as the first thing in `main()`, so everything
below it logs into that session's file. A script or notebook has to ask:

```python
from src import logs

logs.configure(context={"note": "harvest-only run"})

log = logs.get_logger("my-script")
log.info("starting")
```

`context` becomes the header's last line — the settings that decide what the
run will do, so a log read weeks later says what it was a log of. Calling
`configure()` twice returns the first call's path and changes nothing, so
importing a module that configures logging cannot split a session across two
files.

Without `configure()`, nothing breaks: `echo` still prints, `INFO` is
discarded, and `WARNING` and above reach stderr through Python's last-resort
handler.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
`--debug` turns on Flask's reloader, which restarts the process — and a restart
is a new application start, so it opens a **second** log file. It also abandons
any sync in flight, which is why the reloader is off by default.
:::
